card: Enables the `-Wunused` compiler warning flag in CMake and resolves all newly triggered warnings across 136 files, mostly by omitting unused parameter names or adding `[[maybe_unused]]`. Without this warning, dead code accumulates and logic bugs can hide when variables or parameters are unintentionally left unused (as occurred in #36137). The PR depends on upstream Minisketch PR #104 to avoid warnings in vendored code.
changed_since_previous: Rebased with minor adjustments across files while preserving the same three-commit structure.
evidence: PR description cites eleven recent dead code removal PRs (#35679, #35910, #35914, #35971, #36009, #36012, #36103, #36127, #36509, #36706, #36713) that could have been caught by compiler warnings.
PR description points to #36137 as an instance of code that was assumed dead but had actually been mistakenly forgotten.
problem: Bitcoin Core builds without the `-Wunused` warning group, allowing dead code and unused variables to accumulate unnoticed. Unused variables and parameters can also obscure logic errors where variables or inputs were forgotten rather than intentionally ignored.

risk.why: Mechanical changes span sensitive subsystems including consensus and validation, where an erroneous edit or typo could alter execution or cause build breakage.

scope_notes: Large mechanical change across 136 files. Includes a temporary `[[nomerge]]` commit in the vendored minisketch subtree that requires upstreaming.
summary: Enables the `-Wunused` compiler warning flag in CMake and addresses all resulting compiler warnings across the codebase. Across more than 130 files, unused parameters are silenced by removing their names, commenting them out, or annotating them with `[[maybe_unused]]`.
